newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate finalising budget bills.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate finalising budget bills.

text.p: The Australian Senate was finalising consideration of budget bills for 1996 late on Friday, having passed the bulk of the contentious measures in the government's A$7.2 billion fiscal tightening.
However, the upper house amended two social security bills that had contained contentious measures worth A$336 million in the fiscal year to June 1998, their first full year of operation.
The cost of the amendments to the budget was unknown and government officials said it would take days to calculate.
The government also temporarily withdrew one of its major social security measures, a tightening in unemployment benefit eligibility that was to save A$106 million in 1997/98.
Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman told the Senate the measure would be brought back to parliament next year.
Previously, the government had lost in the Senate budget measures worth A$200 million to A$300 million in 1997/98.
The August budget detailed savings worth A$7.2 billion in 1997/98 with the aim of a 1998/99 budget surplus in underlying terms -- that is, without asset sales.
The 1995/96 underlying budget deficit was A$10.3 billion.
Of the A$7.2 billion, roughly A$2.0 billion was put in doubt when the bigger minority parties in the Senate declared their opposition.
However, the bulk of the contentious measures has passed with the support of two independents.
